_comment: Task §25 - predeclared BEFORE observing any QLoRA validation metrics. Timestamped at write time so it is verifiable this was not edited after seeing results.
declaredBeforeSeeing: qlora-baseline-v1 validation metrics (training is in progress; this file was written while only the base-model baseline and a pure-timing 15-step estimate run existed - no QLoRA accuracy/schema numbers of any kind have been observed yet)

unsafeOutputRate.note: Any unsafe output at all is already disqualifying per config/evaluation.yaml's safety gate, independent of this comparison.

schemaValidityRate.note: 0.15 absolute (e.g. 60% -> 75%+) chosen because this is the specific, named product hypothesis (task §30) - a small/noisy delta here specifically should not count as success.

primaryIntentAccuracy.note: Soft gate (task says 'should', not 'must') - a real but smaller improvement here is still informative, not an automatic reject.

inventedEnumRate.note: The single most important measurement per task §30 - did LoRA teach the model to stop inventing Gymini intent/action labels. A real decrease, not merely 'not worse'.

correctionAccuracy.note: 'critical correction/reference must not materially regress' (task §25). Only evaluated over cases where correction is applicable (task's own None-for-not-applicable convention in evaluate_semantics.py).

ambiguityAccuracy.note: Task §9/§31 - a model that gets better at forcing every utterance into an intent, at the cost of correctly saying 'I don't have enough information', is a regression even if other metrics improve.

overallDecisionRule: QLORA_MEANINGFULLY_IMPROVED only if: no hard gate fails, AND inventedEnumRate gate passes, AND schemaValidityRate gate passes, AND no must_not_materially_regress gate fails. QLORA_SMALL_IMPROVEMENT if gates pass but deltas are smaller than the thresholds above. QLORA_REGRESSED if any must_not_worsen/must_not_materially_regress gate fails. Task §31 - schema validity improving while correction/reference/ambiguity quality drops is NOT success, regardless of the weighted product score.
